statement: Prove the identity $\\cos3\\theta=4\\cos^{3}\\theta-3\\cos\\theta$, and hence solve $4x^{3}-3x=\\tfrac{1}{2}$ for $x\\in[-1,1]$.
solution: $\\cos3\\theta=\\cos(2\\theta+\\theta)=\\cos2\\theta\\cos\\theta-\\sin2\\theta\\sin\\theta=(2\\cos^{2}\\theta-1)\\cos\\theta-2\\sin^{2}\\theta\\cos\\theta=2\\cos^{3}\\theta-\\cos\\theta-2(1-\\cos^{2}\\theta)\\cos\\theta=4\\cos^{3}\\theta-3\\cos\\theta$. For the equation set $x=\\cos\\theta\\in[-1,1]$; then $4x^{3}-3x=\\cos3\\theta=\\tfrac{1}{2}$, so $3\\theta=2\\pi k\\pm\\tfrac{\\pi}{3}$. The three distinct values in $[-1,1]$ are $x=\\cos(\\pi/9)$, $x=\\cos(5\\pi/9)$ and $x=\\cos(7\\pi/9)$.
hints: Let x=cos theta to reduce the cubic to cos3theta=1/2.
